outcome: success rate of external cephalic version (ECV)
cohort: Pregnant women who underwent external cephalic version (ECV) at the Hospital Clinico Universitario Virgen de la Arrixaca in Murcia (Spain) between January 1, 2014 and December 31, 2018
finding: This study found that external cephalic version (ECV) was successful in 82.5% of cases, with previous vaginal delivery increasing the success rate and maternal BMI being inversely related to ECV success.
mod_finding: While successful ECV did not significantly affect cesarean or eutocic delivery rates, it was associated with a 6.29% increase in the instrumented delivery rate.
